![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The glob patterns used to find files for Go, Python, and the frontend are incorrect as they only match files in the immediate subdirectory (e.g., `go-app/*.go`) and not in nested directories. This means staged files in subdirectories will be missed by the formatters and linters.

You should use patterns that match files in subdirectories. A portable way to do this without relying on `globstar` is to check for the directory prefix and file suffix separately.

This same issue applies to the Python file check on line 98 and the frontend file check on lines 130-134.

```
for f in "${STAGED_FILES[@]:-}"; do
  if [[ "$f" == go-app/* && "$f" == *.go ]]; then
    GO_FILES_ARR+=("$f")
  fi

```

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

There's a data contract mismatch between the frontend and backend. The backend API was updated to return `match_date` in the `BacktestCandidate` object, but the frontend code here (and the corresponding type in `src/types.ts`) still expects a `date` property. This will cause `c.date` to be `undefined` at runtime, leading to an error when `new Date(c.date)` is called.

Please update the frontend `BacktestCandidate` type and all its usages to use `match_date`.

```suggestion
              <TableCell>{new Date(c.match_date).toISOString().slice(0, 10)}</TableCell>
```

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg) Similar to the issue in `CandidatesTable.tsx`, there is a data contract mismatch here. The backend API was updated to return `match_date` in the `match` object of the `BacktestEvaluateResponse`, but the frontend code is still trying to access `result.match.date`. This will result in a runtime error. Please update the frontend code and the corresponding type in `src/types.ts` to use `match_date`. ```suggestion {new Date(result.match.match_date).toISOString().slice(0, 10)} ```

![security-medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/security-medium-priority.svg) ![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The newly added operational and API endpoints (`/ops/*` and `/api/*`) lack any authentication or authorization checks. This allows unauthenticated users to access sensitive system information, including migration history, database statistics, and internal file paths. It also allows them to trigger potentially expensive operations like ML predictions and database-intensive pagination queries. 

**Recommendation:** Implement an authentication and authorization layer (e.g., middleware) to restrict access to these endpoints to authorized administrators only.

![security-medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/security-medium-priority.svg) ![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The `ListMigrations` endpoint uses a user-supplied `page` parameter to calculate a SQL `OFFSET` without an upper bound. An attacker can provide an extremely large `page` value, forcing the database to perform a very expensive offset operation. This can lead to high CPU and IO usage on the database server, potentially causing a Denial of Service (DoS).

**Recommendation:** Implement a maximum allowed offset or switch to keyset-based pagination (using the `id` or `started_at` column) to ensure consistent performance regardless of the page depth.
